evals.prompt: Explain briefly: running tests shows whether a change broke behavior that was already tested.
evals.expected_output: Short text answer; no diagram, HTML or video, and no promise that tests prove there are no bugs.

assertions.text: Short text answer; no diagram, HTML or video, and no promise that tests prove there are no bugs.

evals.prompt: Explain this flow for the project owner: Webhook -> verify the signature -> if invalid, return 401 and write nothing; if valid, look up event_id; if already processed, return 200 without writing again; if not processed, save inside a transaction and return 200 only after the commit succeeds. A save error returns 500 so the sender retries. Produce output that makes the error branches and repeats easy to see.
evals.expected_output: Includes a fitting branch visual; keeps signature, 401, 200, 500, event_id, transaction and the commit order; does not invent the current runtime.

assertions.text: Includes a fitting branch visual; keeps signature, 401, 200, 500, event_id, transaction and the commit order; does not invent the current runtime.

evals.prompt: Write the requirements section of a plan from this undecided sentence: Only managers can edit recent appointments. There is no other code or documentation.
evals.expected_output: Finds that manager, scope, edit permission and 'recent' are unclear and asks for the needed decisions; does not set 24 hours or 7 days on its own; does not mark the plan ready to code.

assertions.text: Finds that manager, scope, edit permission and 'recent' are unclear and asks for the needed decisions; does not set 24 hours or 7 days on its own; does not mark the plan ready to code.

evals.prompt: Rewrite more clearly, keeping the meaning: Proposal: reduce the timeout from 30s to 10s if the trial passes. The service may be slow on a weak network; this case has NOT been tested yet. The project owner chose SQLite; keep that choice.
evals.expected_output: Keeps 'proposal', 30s/10s, the trial condition, 'may', 'not tested yet' and SQLite.

assertions.text: Keeps 'proposal', 30s/10s, the trial condition, 'may', 'not tested yet' and SQLite.

evals.prompt: --visual off: Compare option A, writing data immediately (simple, a failure may leave data out of sync), with option B, writing through a queue (more operations work, has retries). Compare in text only.
evals.expected_output: No table, diagram or HTML; still covers the trade-offs and keeps the certainty.

assertions.text: No table, diagram or HTML; still covers the trade-offs and keeps the certainty.

evals.prompt: --check --visual html: Review input-plan.md and suggest better wording. Do not edit or create files.
evals.expected_output: Reads the source, reports the ambiguous places and suggestions, does not create HTML or edit the source.

assertions.text: Reads the source, reports the ambiguous places and suggestions, does not create HTML or edit the source.

evals.prompt: --strict: Rewrite in English without changing meaning: The service may respond slowly if the network is unstable. This scenario has not been tested. The timeout remains 30s unless the owner approves a change.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the possible slowness, 'not tested', 30s and the owner condition; does not turn 'may' into 'will'; does not claim compliance with the standard.

assertions.text: Keeps the possible slowness, 'not tested', 30s and the owner condition; does not turn 'may' into 'will'; does not claim compliance with the standard.

evals.prompt: --visual html: Create a self-contained HTML page that illustrates two hypothetical scenarios: processing immediately takes 1s; processing through a queue takes 3s and has retries. Let the user pick a scenario to see the difference. No network calls and no added data.
evals.expected_output: Interactive HTML with exactly the two assumptions, marked as assumptions, no CDN, no invented real rules and no video.

assertions.text: Interactive HTML with exactly the two assumptions, marked as assumptions, no CDN, no invented real rules and no video.
